name: Camera glasses
title: Why Google Glass failed, and why camera glasses sell now
question: Why did Google Glass fail, and when did camera glasses start selling?
answer: Google Glass sold to consumers as a $1,500 Explorer Edition from 2013 and stopped in January 2015 amid a privacy backlash; the enterprise edition ended in 2023. North, maker of Focals, was bought by Google in 2020. Ray-Ban Meta glasses (2023), with a camera and an assistant but no display, passed 2 million sales by February 2025, and EssilorLuxottica sold 7 million Meta glasses in 2025 alone.
verdict_reason: Social acceptance of always-present cameras and cheap on-device AI arrived by 2023.

constraint.name: Social norm around face-worn cameras
constraint.detail: Glass named its own blocker: people around the wearer objected. A product that looks like ordinary glasses changed that.

crossing.text: Ray-Ban Meta launches in late 2023; over 2 million sold by February 2025 (EssilorLuxottica).

graveyard.name: Google Glass (consumer)

graveyard.name: North (Focals)

EssilorLuxottica: 7 million Ray-Ban and Oakley Meta smart glasses sold in 2025, more than triple 2024.
